title: Ranthambore Safari Bookings Crash as Record Demand Overwhelms New Portal
excerpt: Rajasthan's revamped booking website for India's most popular tiger reserve buckled under massive traffic as the October–December season opened, highlighting surging wildlife tourism demand.
body:
• Rajasthan's new forestrajasthan.com booking portal for Ranthambore Tiger Reserve crashed repeatedly when October–December 2026 advance bookings opened on August 1.
  • The reserve welcomed a record 727,268 tourists in the 2024–25 season, generating ₹72 crore in revenue — a ₹12 crore jump from the previous year.
  • The new portal replaced the old OBMS system, which was plagued by bogus bookings and agent manipulation, according to NDTV.
  • With 80-plus tigers and limited daily safari slots — 20 jeeps and 20 canters per shift — demand now vastly outstrips supply.

When advance safari bookings for Ranthambore Tiger Reserve's October–December 2026 season opened at noon on August 1, thousands of wildlife enthusiasts logged on simultaneously — and the portal buckled. Rajasthan's new booking website, forestrajasthan.com, crashed multiple times under the deluge of traffic, leaving would-be visitors refreshing blank screens and fielding error messages.

By the time the site stabilised hours later, many gypsy (jeep) safari slots for prime tiger zones had already sold out, according to travellers posting on TripAdvisor forums.

A New System, Same Old Bottleneck

The crash exposed the sheer scale of demand for India's most storied tiger reserve. The Rajasthan Forest Department had launched forestrajasthan.com in mid-2025 to replace the earlier Online Booking Management System (OBMS), which was officially discontinued on July 14, 2025. The old platform had drawn persistent complaints of bogus bookings, opaque allocation, and agent manipulation that shut out genuine tourists.

"There was no transparency in the earlier system. For a resident of Ranthambore like me, it was impossible to get a booking myself. Certain people would block all the bookings."

— Balendu Singh, Ranthambore hotelier and conservationist, speaking to NDTV

The new portal requires visitors to upload full identity documents — Aadhaar and PAN card for Indians, passport for foreigners — with AI-based verification before a booking is confirmed. Chief Conservator of Forests Arijit Banerjee told NDTV that the system ensures "a higher degree of transparency and efficiency" and keeps up with global technical practices.

Yet the site's infrastructure has struggled to match the reform's ambition. As of August 4, the booking portal displayed a message reading: "All bookings have been paused by the department! The system is undergoing scheduled updates and will be available soon."

Record Tourism Fuels the Frenzy

The booking chaos is a direct consequence of Ranthambore's surging popularity. The reserve welcomed a record 727,268 tourists during the 2024–25 season through May 2025, including 197,146 foreign visitors and 529,693 domestic travellers, according to data published by the park administration. Revenue hit ₹72.49 crore — up ₹12 crore from the previous year.

With more than 80 tigers roaming its dry deciduous forests and strategically placed waterholes offering some of the highest sighting probabilities in India, Ranthambore has cemented its status as the country's premier wildlife destination. The park's proximity to the Delhi–Jaipur highway — roughly five hours by road from the capital — makes it a favoured weekend getaway.

Supply Cannot Keep Up

The mismatch between demand and supply is stark. Only 20 jeeps and 20 canters are permitted per safari shift, spread across 10 zones. Core zones 1 through 5 close on Wednesdays, while zones 6 through 10 close on Tuesdays. Under the new system, advance bookings open in quarterly batches — October–December slots on August 1, January–March on November 1, and April–June on February 1 — all at noon IST.

The compressed booking windows create a situation akin to India's notoriously competitive railway tatkal system: tens of thousands of users competing for a few hundred slots the moment they go live.

"The website has already crashed a couple times due to too much traffic. When I accessed the website several hours later, some dates and some gypsy sessions are already sold out."

— International tourist posting on TripAdvisor's Ranthambore forum

Travellers who miss the advance window face limited options: a premium tatkal quota that opens five days before the safari date at roughly ₹19,000 per jeep, or a current-day canter quota at standard rates — both subject to availability.

What's Next

The Forest Department has said it plans to extend the new booking system to all national parks in Rajasthan from October 1. Whether the platform's server capacity will be upgraded to handle the demand remains to be seen. For now, many travellers continue to rely on local agents and hotel operators to navigate the booking maze — the very intermediaries the new system was designed to bypass.

Ranthambore reopens for the season on October 1 after its annual monsoon closure. The frenzy for bookings suggests the reserve's next chapter will be its busiest yet.
nri_angle: NRIs and international tourists planning India wildlife trips face the same booking gridlock, with the new portal requiring passport uploads and foreign cards often failing on Indian payment gateways.
author: Diaspora Desk
